"Is #Rheumatoid #Arthritis Hereditary?" We should ask about family history of #RA but why? Read on for more  There is a genetic component to the development of RA, meaning that individuals with certain genetic variations may be more likely to develop the disease. There are several genetic variations that have been associated with an increased risk of developing rheumatoid arthritis (RA). These variations are located in genes that are involved in the immune system and inflammation However, genetics is only one factor in the development of RA. Environmental and lifestyle factors also play a role. Asking about Family History is important but only makes up a part of the clinical reasoning process when suspecting Rheumatoid Arthritis. We are looking for first degree relatives with diagnosed RA Want to ask a question or learn more? People don't understand what they cannot see Emotional abuse and auto immune diseases are invisible and therefore both completely misunderstood. So if you haven't been through it you don't necessarily understand it. But I do understand ALL OF IT So if you're after some support but no-one understands or thinks your imagining everything. "Is it #osteoarthritis flare or #gout of the 1st MTP joint?" A common question, let's explore the answer 👇👇👇 Onset of Gout in the first MTPJ is often at night without any overt triggering event. An Osteoarthritis flare will usually be proceeded by an increase in load such as more walking or a new hobby. Gout symptoms will escalate peaking after a few hours, early episodes will resolve after 2-7 days. Osteoarthritis symptoms tend to increase with activity and a flare can last from a few days to 12 weeks. Gout usually has strong inflammatory features (redness, heat, swelling, stiffness). Osteoarthritis has inflammatory features less commonly and at a lower severity (not super red, a little warm, a little swollen, stiffness for up to 15 mins in the morning) Uric Acid levels are more likely to be raised in Gout, just as x-ray changes associated with 1st MTPJ Osteoarthritis are more likely in OA. There is significant overlap and coexistance. Want to ask a question or learn more? Ignore the pessimists! ✋ Taking proactive steps to enhance your quality of life is crucial. If others insist there's no room for improvement through healthy lifestyle changes, remember that's their limitation, not yours. While medication has its merits when necessary, it shouldn't be your sole reliance. Embracing healthy lifestyle changes will undeniably yield long-term benefits. Transforming your diet, adjusting habits, and incorporating exercise will foster an optimal environment for your healing journey. Typically associated with goals like achieving a beach-ready body or looking stunning in a dress, a healthy lifestyle extends beyond aesthetics. It means: 👉 Having more energy to play with your kids 👉 Enjoying higher-quality time with friends 👉 Boosting emotional fitness 👉 Gaining increased physical strength 👉 Enhancing appetite 👉 Improving sleep 👉 Promoting better bone health 👉 Lowering disease activity And much more! 'Just take the first step' To many people sit around complaining of things they dont have yet do nothing to show for it Could go for a lot of things but this case is health  How often have you heard from your doctors that getting your steps in , drinking more water , going to the gym , eating better is hard for you? All these factors will contribute towards how you feel Having a stronger mind set or a better physique will add towards the feeling of the meds working for you Doesn't have to be eveything at once. Walk more for a week see how you feel. There's one win... Week after walk more or even drink more water. There's a second win... Week 3 , maybe start swapping the odd thing in your diet. Third win... All little changes but do this for a long time and you'll be a totally different version of yourself come 3 months , 6 months, maybe even a year if you stick it out... #crohnsdisease #crohns #invisibleillness #medications #nhs #colitis #ibd #ibs #healthconditions #immunesystem #autoimmunedisease #diseases

My tips for if you’ve just been diagnosed with Crohn’s disease or Ulcerative colitis  1- Track everything you’re eating and get a food diary  2- Learn about the stool chart and track your bowl movements  3- Invest in a good heat source  4- Don’t compare your IBD to anyone else’s  6- Join the Crohn’s and Colitis UK forum page on Facebook  7- Minimise the amount of alcohol your drinking and try to quit smoking  8- Avoid ibuprofen and Imodium  If you have any more tips please put them in the comments. Happy IBD awareness week💜 #ibd #crohns #colitis

👉🏻 CROHNS CREW 👈🏻 Struggling with your meds? I got you 👇🏻 Recently asked 'What would I do if my meds stopped working for me' so here it is  1) First off I'd do everything I could to get in touch with my specialist as we all know how hard that can be for starters. Emails , calls , voice messages the full lot. Give it a week or so and you should get a reply 📲 2) Tell them EVERYTHING. Don't brush off your symptoms when they finally reply and say something along the lines 'ah I'm not too bad , just the odd blah blah blah'. Tell them all the problems you've got or are having, with as much detail as you can. Tell them how it affects you mentally , physically and how it disrupts your day to day life 📝 3) Do your own research - not in the sense where you diagnose yourself like we all do when ill 👀 In the sense of what meds could I try next , then mention that to your specialist too ' I like the sound of...' 'would x med work' 'whats the pros of x med'. The more knowledge you have on yourself and your own meds the less likely people will push you to a side 💻 To some things up , do your research and dont be afraid to ask questions, otherwise they'll work down their list with their trial and error meds hoping one works and tell you to come back in 12 weeks time. Example of something working for me was when they tried to get me on humeria god knows how many times or something similar to it (brain fog) , read all the symptoms, really didn't fancy trying it as it was my last option before surgery and I was sick of being ill. 6 months later , stoma operation done , med free feeling 100x better 🤷‍♂️ You's will get there for sure 👊🏻 #crohnsandcolitis #crohnscolitisuk  #crohnsdisease #crohns #colitis #stoma #ibd #ibs

#CrohnsCrew ⬅️ Most of us are constantly going to be in a bad spot for a while at somepoint in life. You's can either accept it or embrace it head on and give yourself the best chance of getting through things  - Showing up when you cant be bothered  - Eating better  - Exercising  - Chasing for new meds  - Doing the small daily tasks to feel better  Do whatever you need to do to get the momentum going , promise you you'll start to feel better  'Oh but I'm just going to get ill again whats the point' Need to do things over and over and over for a very long time. Mindset is everything when ill , if you have a weak one you'll no doubt continue to stay ill Train your mind just as much as you would your body and watch how things start to improve #crohnsandcolitis #crohnscolitis #crohnsdisease #crohns #colitis #ibs #ibd #stoma #ileostomybag #ileostomy #colostomy #colostomybag #stomabag #invisibleillness  #hospital #healthandfitness

📣 Crohns Crew Here's how to change your future 📣 If someone had said a few years ago I'd of travelled around the East Coast of Australia I'd of proabably laughed  Before my operation I was in a pretty bad way physically and mentally , hated how life was , couldn't do anything I enjoyed and even when I did it was a struggle and I couldn't quite enjoy myself how I should of  I'd always make excuses to get out of things or even just ignore the fact stuff was happening  Would always try play football, exercise eat well in the off chance it would help...yet nothing  Fast forward a few years , I get the stoma operation and I start to feel me again. I can eat what I want , go where I want , do whatever I want. Yeah sometimes fatigue hit but it wasn't anywhere near to how bad it was.  Could finally start to live life the way I wanted it  Anyways... 6 years it took , 6 YEARS...to get to the stage of feeling truly happy with things  It might take you weeks , months or years but I promise there's a way around things for everyone, you just have to try different things and push for other solutions  Yeah my time in Aus short and I wish I had did some things differently. But it wasn't till I was due to come back where a few mates reminded me how far I've really came and because of that it's made me appreciate the jounrey , the people I've met and everything in between that little bit more So if anyones struggling, push for that new medication, tell GPs how you really feel. Dont settle for something they're forcing on you if you dont want to do it. You know your body more than they do. I asked 100s of times for my stoma operation and even turned down meds on the way and it was all worth it to be where I am now This could be you one day , enjoying the things you want to do 🙏🏻 #crohnscolitisuk #crohnsdisease #crohns #crohnsandcolitis #crohnsandcolitisuk #colitis #ibd #ibs #stoma #stomabag #colostomy #colostomybag #ileostomybag #ileostomy #invisibleillness #healthiswealth #mindset

👉🏻 CROHNS CREW 👈🏻 Struggling with your meds? I got you 👇🏻 Recently asked 'What would I do if my meds stopped working for me' so here it is  1) First off I'd do everything I could to get in touch with my specialist as we all know how hard that can be for starters. Emails , calls , voice messages the full lot. Give it a week or so and you should get a reply 📲 2) Tell them EVERYTHING. Don't brush off your symptoms when they finally reply and say something along the lines 'ah I'm not too bad , just the odd blah blah blah'. Tell them all the problems you've got or are having, with as much detail as you can. Tell them how it affects you mentally , physically and how it disrupts your day to day life 📝 3) Do your own research - not in the sense where you diagnose yourself like we all do when ill 👀 In the sense of what meds could I try next , then mention that to your specialist too ' I like the sound of...' 'would x med work' 'whats the pros of x med'. The more knowledge you have on yourself and your own meds the less likely people will push you to a side 💻 To some things up , do your research and dont be afraid to ask questions, otherwise they'll work down their list with their trial and error meds hoping one works and tell you to come back in 12 weeks time. Example of something working for me was when they tried to get me on humeria god knows how many times or something similar to it (brain fog) , read all the symptoms, really didn't fancy trying it as it was my last option before surgery and I was sick of being ill. 6 months later , stoma operation done , med free feeling 100x better 🤷‍♂️ You's will get there for sure 👊🏻 #crohnsandcolitis #crohnscolitisuk  #crohnsdisease #crohns #colitis #stoma #ibd #ibs

#CrohnsCrew ⬅️ Most of us are constantly going to be in a bad spot for a while at somepoint in life. You's can either accept it or embrace it head on and give yourself the best chance of getting through things  - Showing up when you cant be bothered  - Eating better  - Exercising  - Chasing for new meds  - Doing the small daily tasks to feel better  Do whatever you need to do to get the momentum going , promise you you'll start to feel better  'Oh but I'm just going to get ill again whats the point' Need to do things over and over and over for a very long time. Mindset is everything when ill , if you have a weak one you'll no doubt continue to stay ill Train your mind just as much as you would your body and watch how things start to improve #crohnsandcolitis #crohnscolitis #crohnsdisease #crohns #colitis #ibs #ibd #stoma #ileostomybag #ileostomy #colostomy #colostomybag #stomabag #invisibleillness  #hospital #healthandfitness

👇🏻 How to start 2024 the right way 👇🏻 1) Real People Around You - by that I mean surround yourself with people who motivate you , push you to be better , could be at gym , a job, whatever...This can be in person or online , if you're scrolling hours a day away and are watching bulls**t content 90% of the time , chances are it's not going to benefit you in anyway.  2) Less Processed Food - This one definitely goes for those with health conditions such as crohns, ibd ect. Do this for a month and chances are you symptoms will reduce, your energy will improve and you'll generally just feel better withing yourself.  3) Gym 3-5x a week - If you can get in better shape whether that be gaining weight , lasting weight , building more muscle AGAIN , you'll feel better withing yourself mentally and physically. You'll also have more confidence, more energy, as well as all the rest of the pros. Doesn't have to be for long , could be 20 minute sessions if you know what you're doing or even just a walk a day to get started 4) 8 Hours Of Sleep - Forget Gary Vee and all the other people who say 'I sleep 4hrs a day and I feel great'. Sleep is probably the most important of them all , especially those with health conditions as chances are you need more than the 'normal' person. You'll feel energised, more focused, fight off other illness to name a few 5) 3+ Litres Of Water - Water is key for hydration (again especially for those with conditions) , helps towards muscles, lose weight , bowel function , kidney health , skin problems and loads more. Throw in some electrolytes the odd time too for even more benefits. 6) More Protein- Finally more protein, doesn't have to be a lot but it will help you towards getting in shape. Can reduce appetite (if losing weight) , repair muscles for growth , help towards skin , blood , bones. And personally for me (aimed at stoma people) I find it the easiest thing to digest which again all loops round into one Pick one to improve each week and in a months time you'll thank yourself, dont rush it all at once though as you'll gas out and give up #crohns #crohnsdisease #crohnsandcolitis #ibd #ibs #colitis #stoma #stomabag #crohnscolitis

It can be as simple as offering them a nice warm drink and a listening ear ☕   If someone you know has Crohn’s or Colitis, the little things you do can make a big difference to them. It can be really hard to know how best to help someone who’s living with Crohn’s or Colitis. You might feel anxious or powerless because you can’t take their condition away. That’s totally natural. The good news is that there are lots of things you can do to help.   Listen to what they’re going through and validate their feelings. Sometimes people might prefer just to carry on as normal and not talk about their illness. But at other times they may appreciate someone to open up to.   It’s important to show that you believe them when they talk about their symptoms, and that they are not a burden to you. Instead of feeling sorry for them, it’s good to take time to really understand what they’re going through. You don’t need to have all the answers, sometimes listening is enough.   #LittleThings #Crohns #Colitis #IBD #ConSantanderConecto

HOW TO TRACK THE BULK ⚖💪🏻 If you're gaining roughly 0.2 - 0.5kg a week you're on the right track (0.4 - 1.1lbs)  Some people prefer the smaller end of the scale meaning you could bulk for longer , stay leaner , build more muscle over time Others prefer a quicker approach will give you pretty similar results just not be able to continue it for as long  I tend to weigh myself daily , roughly between 7:00 and 7:30am after using going to the toilet and before eating/drinking anything  Take note of your weight Then end of the week I'll add them up , find the average by dividing it by how many days I tracked my weight and the number being the weight for the week If thag goes up 0.2kg+ the week after I keep calories the same  If it happens to be the same or less , I'll add a few calories to my weekly total  My weekly total is currently 3000 , possibly be on this for another week or two I imagine then I'll bump it up to 3200 I reckon You can increase your calories from 100-500 calories, depending on your time scale for things  Todays Numbers: Calories - 3027 Protein - 131 Fats - 73 Carbs - 420 ➡️ @ibdliam__ ⬅️ #bulking #winterbulk #bulkingseason #bulk #weightgain #weigthlifting #bodybuilding #gym #fitness #health #healthandfitness #crohns #crohnsdisease #colitis #crohnsandcolitis #ibd #ibs #stoma #stomabag #ileostomy #ileostomybag #Colostomy #Colostomybag

Giving them a lift 🚙  Many people with Crohn’s or Colitis experience fatigue. Fatigue is ongoing tiredness, lack of energy or exhaustion that doesn’t improve even after rest or sleep. Offering a lift so they don’t have to drive or deal with public transport can be a little thing that can enormously help someone with Crohn’s or Colitis.  Some people with Crohn’s or Colitis may need surgery, afterwards, they may feel weak and tired and be unable to do any lifting or driving for a while.  It’s also important to be mindful of toilet access and pit stops when planning car trips or events. People with Crohn’s or Colitis sometimes need to use toilets urgently. Be patient with them if they spend a long time in the toilet, or rush off mid conversation to find the nearest loo. Filling up a hot water bottle 💜 Ask what helps your friend or family member manage their pain. This may be yoga, avoiding certain foods, or taking the right pain medicine. After experiencing a severe Crohn's flare-up, I found myself in a weakened state, having lost weight, muscle tone, and strength. Recognizing the need for movement and recovery, I turned to dynamic pilates as a suitable option. As someone who battles Crohn's and works as a Sports Therapist, I understand the importance of starting slow with rehabilitation after physical setbacks or injuries. Dynamic pilates, being low impact, proved to be an ideal choice for me. Its focus on controlled movements and proper alignment ensured that my joints and muscles were targeted without placing excessive strain on my body. This was particularly crucial for someone recovering from a severe flare-up like mine. Engaging in dynamic pilates allowed me to gradually regain my strength and muscle tone. The exercises were both challenging and gentle, enabling me to work within my limits and progressively build up my endurance. Moreover, it contributed to improving my flexibility, which had been compromised during my time in the hospital. Beyond the physical benefits, dynamic pilates provided me with mental and emotional relief. The mindfulness aspect of the practice allowed me to stay present and concentrate on the movements, offering respite from the stress and worries often associated with chronic illnesses. Overall, dynamic pilates was a crucial part of my recovery journey. It not only helped me regain my physical strength and flexibility but also provided a sense of empowerment and control over my body. I would highly recommend it to anyone going through a similar situation.  #TMacLife #ChronsDisease #Chrons #Colitis #flareup #IBD #recovery #rehab #exerciserehab #womenshealth #SportsTherapy #physicalTherapy

#stophoax Wholewheat dan Refined wheat itu jauh beda nilai nutrisi dan tekstur serta kandungan seratnya!  . Stop Membodohi Masyarakat!  . Saya paham berapa banyak industri makanan yang akan berkurang pendapatannya apabila msyarkat mulai menghindari atau setidaknya mengurangi asupan tepung terigu, tetapi sumpah profesi anda itu untuk menyehatkan masyarakat bukan membuat masyarakat bertambah sakit . Mau nunggu IBD, (Colitis, Crohn's disease) atau Autoimun lambung dan penyakit celiac baru disuruh berhenti makan tepung dan segala turunannya? Anak umur 2-4 tahun masa udah banyak kena IBD 🤯bagaimana masa depannya? obat seumur hidup? . Nunggu sampai obat dan penyakitnya mahal? . Nunggu sampai kekurangan nutrisi kronis gara-gara pencernaan yang berantakan dan peradangan kronis? . Adiksi di masyrakat udah parah, bukan lagi wafer, mie instan, kue, biskuit, mpek-mpek pakai terigu, telor dadar pakai terigu, cabe aja sekarang diteriguin, goreng ikan pakai terigu . Mencegah lebih baik daripada Mengobati . Sekolah tinggi tapi waktu SD nya nggak disuruh bikin kata Mutiara dan dipajang di kelasnya nih seperti jaman saya SD . #temansehatdebby belajar mandiri juga sekarang pakai mata dan isi kepala sendiri, kalau yang mau debat boleh minimal dokter gelarnya atau praktisi ilmi kesehatan kesehatan Komplimenter yang kuliahnya minimal 3 tahun ya . Jangan bawa-bawa Tuhan! Gandum memang tumbuhan banyak nutrisinya, tapi Tuhan tidak menciptakan Glyphosate, pestisida dan Tuhan nggak menyarankan itu gandum digiling, sampai habis seratnya dan nutrisinya sampai makan roti empuk-empuk  . Tepung terigu dan produk olahannya adalah makanan emergency kalau ada perang atau musibah bencana alam, bukan jadi makanan setiap hari dan dikesankan mewah . Itu bahan makanan murah tapi penyakitnya mahal . Salam Sehat Selalu . Remember, if your loved one lives with Crohn’s or Colitis, it’s often the little things that mean a lot.  💜They might be too tired to go out for a meal or anxious about toilet access, so why not consider cooking them a candlelit meal at home?  💜 If their fatigue is hitting hard, a night in with a movie on the sofa might be the perfect Valentine’s date night.  💜 A bunch of flowers, a safe snack and a freshly made hot water bottle might go down a treat too! Bulking With A Stoma Day 35 💪🏻  Had my first partial blockage in a long time  *basically not a full one but my body trying to get rid of eveything it has in it  Probably cos I was f**king on with that shake 🥴😂  Woke up today feeling 💀  Anyways here's how I handle my day if this ever happens as most times it's a write off ⬇️  ➡️ Have a chill day - all night my stoma will be firing out water to try flush the body. Meaning I feel pretty fatigued the next day so if possible I'll have a chill day and do little to no work  ➡️ Go for easy foods - Pick out simple foods , easy snacks , preferably some with salts in as your body would of lost a lot from something like this. Even electorate drinks are a good one. Better yet , get someone to make food for you if you can 🤷‍♂️  ➡️ Lots of water - Again I'll of lost a load of fluids in the short space of time so it's about replacing all of those again. MY STORY: Diagnosed at 40 years old with anal cancer, stage unknown. In February 2022, I was diagnosed with anal cancer after numerous visits to the GP due to severe pain in the anal area, initially thought to be hemorrhoids. This discomfort persisted for about a year, progressively worsening despite treatment with hemorrhoid creams prescribed by the GP. Two months later, I arranged an emergency appointment with the GP as the pain became unbearable. During an internal examination, the GP found no unusual signs despite the presence of protrusions both externally and internally. Expressing my dissatisfaction with the ineffectiveness of the prescribed treatment, I requested urgent cancer tests. Subsequently, I underwent an endoscopy, followed by an immediate CT (or MRI) scan, which revealed a concerning and potentially cancerous finding. Thus began my journey. My oncologist determined the cancer to be anal, extending outside the anus and causing substantial bowel damage, leading to fecal incontinence. Despite initial reluctance, I underwent stoma surgery before commencing intense radiotherapy and chemotherapy in April 2022. The chemotherapy caused severe adverse reactions, resulting in hospitalization for a week. Contrary to expectations, I lost my hair entirely. Pelvic radiotherapy caused third-degree burns, leaving me bedridden for three weeks and enduring ongoing radiation cystitis. Despite completing treatment, persistent bleeding and pain necessitated further surgery. On February 16, 2023, I underwent APR surgery, lasting over ten hours. The extensive procedure involved removing my rectum, vagina, part of the bowel, and reconstructing the pelvic floor muscle. Complications arose post-surgery, requiring emergency procedures to address tissue necrosis, leaving me with a sizable open wound requiring daily care. Recovery proved arduous, with months spent bedridden and enduring excruciating pain managed with potent medications. The loss of my vagina, contrary to assurances, has been emotionally devastating. Now, over a year post-surgery, I still require daily wound care but find solace in my remission and gradual improvement. Throughout this journey, the unwavering support of my partner and father has been invaluable. I was confident, had the most beautiful long thick hair, I was a size 10 and healthy. I stayed to bleed 20-30 times a day but was fobbed off for months. Until I developed sepsis and my body was giving up. I had 9 blood clots in my body. I was rushed to hospital finally where they found all along I had crohns disease. Years I had battled with so many bowel issues and years I was told 'you have ibs' or 'you may just need to do less'.. until my life could have been over. I lost everything within. I lost my weight and hit 6 stone in 2 months from being 10 stone. I lost my hair. I lost my mind and developed PTSD. I already have bipolar disorder so this was a huge hit on my mental health. I was always so outgoing and confident but I lose it all. I was hospitalised for many weeks. I lose my mobility which I got back within 2 months. I felt guilty I wasn't being the mum I always was. I live and breath my son. I lost it all.  I am still facing struggles but my hair is growing with treatment, my weight has come back on with fresubins and my confidence is creeping back. Mostly, I'm being the mum I always was.  I am awaiting for an appointment to have colostomy bag permanently to give me my quality of life back.  This disease is hard and never spoken about. I want to support and try and reassure anyone with this disease that we CAN and we WILL beat this.  #crohns #colitis #awareness

Bulking Series Day 40 💪🏻 Having quite a sluggish day this morning, few stomach cramps Whether this is food related or something else who knows Whenever I feel like this for me , a hot drink helps flush my body a bit  As well as sticking to more liquid calories, I find these are a lot easier to digest and takes the body very little effort  I'll do this normally just for a few hours then I feel back to my normal ways Be carful on liquid shakes though as with mine I'll add fruit/milk which are two things that gives bloating to a lot of others with IBD  Whats your go to food/meal when struggling with something? one of the biggest challenges with big weight loss (especially unintended) is mental adapting to the changes of what you see in the mirror. seeing someone who is large for a long time change (size 20-22) so sudden to someone a size 10-12 is something I'd never have thought would be a struggle. but it is. every time someone says you're so slim, wow I'd love to lose weight like you have, well done keep going, but not realise I've done nothing. I've become ill. I'd have loved to have lost weight the normal way but it never happened for me. it was only through extreme pain, embarrassing stints of urgency to go to the toilet, not being able to leave the house, the bed at times that have made me lose weight. the chronic pain, fatigue and the sickness have made me feel more unhealthy than when I was large.  but these words from people are always without malice or harmful intentions. they saw my struggles before becoming unwell and only wanted to spur me on to be the best version of myself I strived so long for. little did I realise that being slim isn't the only goal, being healthy is.  but now I'm working on becoming well. pushing for what I need to become the best version of me because I still see the really round, really large me still. I still see the girl who is described as chubby, plump and 'on the big side'. but that's ok she can still walk with me as a reminder but one day we will find the new me. and when we do we can all walk with a head held high that despite the friends lost because I 'wasn't there' or that distance themselves, I have people who care and I'm learning to care. for big me, small me, old me and new me. having bowel disease has been the most tiring strenuous thing I've ever encountered but I'm determined to not let it rule my life. This is some of my head & neck cancer journey, 2yrs squeezed into 35 images as tt will not allow me anymore so I will upload more asap. Id like to take this opportunity to thank You all so much for your patience & of course your support. My earlier video last year received almost 1 MILLION views & I may of saved 2 lifes, my intentions & hopes was to raise awareness and i did. Is also like to thank TT for allowing me a platform to accomplish this. My journey has been massively complicated & comprised by a failing bowel, this was diagnosed within the same week or so as my head & neck cancer. Completely unrelated just very unfortunate and rotten luck. The initial plan after the tonsillectomy was to have further surgery for radical neck dissection to remove between 50-70 lymph nodes and dependent on that, if cancer was found in any of these nodes I would have radiotherapy. But first before any cancer treatment I had to have urgent surgery on my bowel as it stopped working due to a blockage and a severe colitis flare-up. Some bowel was removed and a ileostomy was performed. Unfortunately this went terribly wrong, the ileostomy was successful however within days I herniated & this caused strangulation and the stoma was compromised. I had to undergo emergency surgery once again. This then lead to a serious infection and many months in hospital fighting sepsis. After 3 pre-assessments were arranged & each time unable to attend a different hospital that specialised in head & neck cancer. They did not have a surgical/colorectal team to assist with my care. The surgery I required was a lengthy 7-9 hour operation followed by specialist intensive care & due to my unstable bowel they did not have the facilities to deal with my bowel and I was deemed a high risk patient and to unwell. I begged them worried sick cancer would kill me, but sadly this surgery would of put my life at risk. My only option was to pray i recovered as soon as possible and my bowel to stabalise then to have radiotherapy. This eventuality happened in August, 6 months after being diagnosed with tonsil cancer. It has been incredibly hard and a very long and slow recovery. I am still recovering now, 1.5yrs after completing radiotherapy i still have allot of issues. Under the watchful eye of ENT, Macmillan speech & language therapy.. dieticians and many more, combined therapy. My main issue is still my bowel and in January this year I underwent a massive operation to repair a huge parastomal hernia. I had a laparotomy cut from the top of my abdomen to the bottom. I had a stoma reversal on the right & a new ilieostomy on the left. This seen me 1 week in ICU followed by 7 weeks in a surgical ward. I was discharged March 11th and re-admitted a few days later with a burst abcess which happened at home. I was discharged a few days later and district nurses visiting every 2 days to pack a small hole but a deep sinus track to heal from inside out. Approximately 2 weeks later things again went wrong and on Tuesday (09th April 2024) I again underwent emergency surgery to re-open my abdomen and now have a very large hole/cavity around the size of the palm of my hand and will be left open needing packed daily in hope it heals from the inside to out. Providing all goes well im looking at months of daily care.  This video is about my cancer but i also wanted to share with You my current situation. I will be uploading further videos in the next few days about my bowel. This has been my reason for my lack of communication and the reason i did not share my cancer journey as promised in 2022. Thank You again for your patience & support, & please reach out for help if anything looks untowards. These last 4 years have been rough… From being that one healthy person.. to have my world turn upside down. I’ve been through a lot..  Multiple internal bleeds,  Ulcerative Colitis  Double pneumonia Failing Kidneys  Failing Liver  Multiple tears/holes in my lungs  Failed treatment..  Lung infections  Kidney infections Stomach infections  Intestinal infections  Blood transfusions  Iron infusions  And so much more I don’t wish to share..  In December 2021.. I was prepared to pass away in hospital due to my health severely declining. I couldn’t breathe without oxygen, my lungs had started to shut down, my liver & kidneys weren’t working. I was bed bound.. I couldn’t change my own clothes.. I couldn’t take myself to the toilet.. I couldn’t walk and I struggled to speak due to my lungs. I suffered severe panic attacks due to not being able to breathe.. and you really understand in those moments that you can feel the end is near.  I was lucky to make it out of there. I’ve witnessed some horrible things.. including people passing away in front of me. These things really do change you as a person and it haunts you. Anything can happen in a blink of an eye..  I’m on medication that keeps my organs from attacking themselves which also makes me immunosuppressed. I can get an infection from the smallest of things.. even a cut on my finger can cause my entire body to be riddled with a life threatening infection. It’s hard to deal with.  But I will continue to fight my battles no matter what happens.  #journey #ulcerativecolitis #colitis #story #mystory #mentalhealth #son #fighting #hospital #fyp #fypシ #fypシ゚viral #foryoupage

Between early 2021 & late 2022 I suffered many small bowel blockages and many colitis flare-ups which my surgeon & i thought was the cause, many operations were done in this time as I was very poorly each blockage getting more aggressive. It wasnt until late 2021 we soon realised my bowel was failing & failing fast, my large bowel was barely functioning and many medications were tried in order to stimulate it but to no avail. In February 2022 my health was further compromised when I was diagnosed with tonsil cancer, totally unrelated just very rotten luck. The decision was quickly made by my colorectal surgeon to have surgery and a ileostomy was performed immediately so I could have treatment for head & neck cancer. I already had a tonsillectomy in early February and the biopsies revealed the cancer. Fearful the cancer may of spread locally it was decided I was to have a neck dissection asap but i first needed to recover from stoma surgery. Unfortunately my luck got worse and i herniated a few days after surgery, the small hernia had to be operated on urgently as it was strangulating my bowel restricting flow. This then lead to a severe infection and sepsis was diagnosed. Desperate to get me out of hospital asap more surgery was performed. My oncologist & colorectal surgeon were liasing daily as time was against me. I was in hospital for around 2 months as i healed very slowly, my body was not only fighting this infection it was fighting head & neck cancer. I was offered a pre-assessment, a specialist hospital around 30 miles away was to perform the neck dissection to remove between 50-70 lymph nodes. This pre-assessment came & went  as I was admitted back into hospital under the surgical team for further bowel issues. Oncology tried to comfort me reminding me the main tumour had been removed but knowing the severity of cancer I definitely couldnt take comfort in ‘hear say’ I was once again operated on but this time the wound completely broke down after a new end ileostomy was performed getting rid of the loop ileostomy, once again infection dominated my recovery. Another pre-assesment came and went, i found myself begging East Grinstead the hospital that was to perform the neck disection not to give up on me, this operation was my best chance of ridding the disease and facing a better outcome… life! Fast forward a few months I was finally fit for discharge & I made the 3rd pre-assessment. I had bloods taken, an ECG was performed, basic observations like bp and heart rate were all done and finally the chat with the anaesthetist. I came away from this appointment possitive as I believed everything went perfectly. Little did I know the decision had already been made and I received a call from my oncologist the next morning. Thinking back that conversation hit me more than the one in February surrounded my macmillan nurses being told I had cancer. The oncologist broke the news to me saying how sorry he was and little to nothing he could do about the outcome, the neck disection was refused. The anaesthetist having the final say said I was unfit for this long complicated surgery. He said I was deemed high risk taking into account many factors like my unstable bowel and my heart failure. I have LBBB & dilated cardiomyopathy, should I of had complications in theatre or high dependancy I would of required transport to another hospital as they did not have a surgical team to deal with my bowel & no one likes dealing with a patient in heart failure albeit stable. The conversation after that was short, I spent months longing this surgery to be denied. My only option was radiotherapy, my worst nightmare spending months talking to head & neck cancer survivors who had been through radiotherapy. For anyone unsure about head & neck radiotherapy pop onto the Macmillan head & neck cancer website. Dear Eddie Abbew. I honestly didn’t want to make this video. Talking about Crohns disease is not fun for me. For people who love Eddie Abbew, this video will inevitably be perceived as me being a “hater”, and some of them will get angry at me for having a difference of opinion. In some ways, making a response video is not worth the stress and just puts more eyeballs on the original video, which I do not want. But, this topic is too near and dear to my heart for me to just see it and keep scrolling. I am not only someone with Crohn’s disease, but I am also someone who delayed medical care because I secretly hoped I could fix myself via an appropriate diet and healthy lifestyle. I have tried all kinds of different dietary approaches. Eating more of some foods, eating less of some foods, avoiding some foods completely. Symptomatically, dietary changes can help me a lot. But, implying that you should ignore medical advice and refuse medication in favour of eating a specific diet is so misguided it borderlines on criminal. This isn’t just vague dietary advice to eat a more nutritious diet. This is the kind of specific advice that can literally land people in hospital. Are there people who report benefits from it? Sure, but you can also say that with any diet, including celery juice cleanses. It’s not an excuse to give blanket advice to everyone. Please, if you are desperate, I understand wanting to try everything. But listening to people spewing unqualified dietary advice for your medical circumstances can be a very, very dangerous game. That’s my piece. I am not here to argue. And that’s okay!  Healing is a journey, not a destination.  It's about progress, not perfection. Forget the "perfect" version of yourself.  Focus on how far you've come!  Remember that feeling incredibly poorly?  You're not there anymore.  Celebrate the improvements, big and small. Here's the truth:  healing isn't linear.  There will be good days and bad days.  But focusing on setbacks as failures only sets you back. Think of it like a spectrum.  On one end, you have "incredibly poorly,"  and on the other,  your version of  "healed," "remission," or "symptom-free."   You have control over some aspects of this journey. Focus on the things you CAN control: 👉 Healthy habits: Eating well, getting enough sleep, and managing stress are all crucial for healing. 👉 Medical care: Work with your doctor to create a treatment plan that supports your goals. 👉 Positive mindset: Believe in yourself and your ability to heal. Taking control of these aspects empowers you to  move steadily towards your desired state.  It may not happen overnight, but with consistent effort, you'll get there. Remember:  You are stronger than you think.   Keep moving forward, one healthy step at a time. There are more than 500,000 people in the UK living with Crohn’s or Colitis. That's 25,000 people a year who are given the life changing diagnosis of Inflammatory Bowel Disease. It’s a sizeable chunk of the population, but despite this, there are often myths and misconceptions surrounding these conditions, which feed stigmas, hinder understanding, and undermine the severity of symptoms experienced by those living with Crohn's or Colitis. That's why, in the run up to World IBD Day, we’re highlighting some of the most popular misconceptions people have about Crohn’s and Colitis and setting the record straight. Have you ever found yourself in a conversation where you're met with the myth - 'It's not that bad, it's just a dodgy tummy right?'. Crohn’s and Colitis involves chronic inflammation of the gut, which can lead to damage and ulcers. When your gut doesn’t work properly, the effects can be devastating. Crohn’s and Colitis can disrupt every part of your life - from digestion and joints to your energy levels and mental health. There can also be severe complications such as strictures (narrowing of the intestines), fistulas (abnormal connections between different parts of the intestines or between the intestines and other organs) and abscesses – all of which are incredibly painful. Often people living with Crohn’s or Colitis describe the intense pain as ‘someone tying their innards in a knot’. This World IBD Day 🌍 help us correct the widespread misunderstanding, so no one feels ignored or dismissed because of their Crohn's or Colitis. 💩⛔️TW-OPEN STOMA SIGHT⛔️💩 Happy world IBD day! 💪💜  Im sorry to anyone struggling right now. Unless you have crohns or colitis. You could never understand the suffering it entails. It isnt just problems 💩. Its agonising pain, fatigue, malnutrition. The list goes on. This story is a postive one though. I mean if you see the bright side of loosing 6 foot of your intestines, and half of your bowel 😂 I know not everyone can say the same. So lets hope one day that we can find a cure for this awful disease!  But, for the “unlucky ones” like me. I thought my life was was over. 21 years old, suddenly a single mum with two toddlers and whole new way of living. I didnt know i had Crohn’s disease, until i woke up after 7 days in an induced coma. With a stoma. I DIDNT EVEN KNOW WHAT A STOMA WAS. Its hard to say now, but i didnt know if I even wanted to be alive… after i had just been saved😢. Back to the positive side of this story though. I made it. I recoved. It gave me strength to eat and drink being sick. Gave my girls their mummy back, and If that wasnt good enough. I met the love of my absolute life. A man who loved me, and still loves me unconditionally. YES EVEN WITH A 💩BAG. If thats not a real man then im not sure what is 😂 We blended our family, and added another! Built a life together. One I just love so much ❤️ Living with this disease, is not easy of course. And I could sit and dwell over what I happened to me. Somedays I do. I’m reminded everyday when i see my body and scars, of the trauma i did go though. But if it wasnt for them, and my stoma. I wouldn’t have made it here today. "No amount of vegetables and no amount of avoiding pizza, pasta, takeaways or chocolate is going to cure me of a lifelong illness that I can't get rid of. Unfortunately however, that narrative is something that's very much alive and well."   Lauren @lauren_talking_shite was diagnosed with Crohn’s Disease in 2018 after five years of unexplained symptoms. She explains why she finds myths around diet so frustrating, and how when people give unsolicited advice they usually mean really well, but unfortunately it can do more harm than good.   If you have Crohn’s or Colitis, what you eat may affect your symptoms. But it is different for everybody. There’s no one-size-fits-all advice on diet. There is no evidence that following a particular diet can cure Crohn’s or Colitis. You may come across diets that claim to do this, but there is no proof that these work.   Want to get involved in myth-busting this World IBD Day? “My symptoms will vary from the worst joint pains, to deep, deep abdominal cramps, which are so painful they're often nauseating. And, I guess the worst part in all of this is that no one would know anything was happening because having Crohn's or Colitis is an invisible disease." Actor and Crohn's & Colitis UK Ambassador Sacha Dhawan has lived with Crohn's Disease for many years now. It took him a while to come to terms with his condition and speak openly about what he was going through. As Sacha mentions in the clip above,  Crohn’s and Colitis are invisible illnesses. They often cause symptoms that other people won’t see, such as severe pain, diarrhoea, blood in poo or extreme tiredness. Living with Crohn’s or Colitis can be hard, but this may not be noticeable to other people. Not everyone’s symptoms are the same. Although Crohn’s and Colitis are types of Inflammatory Bowel Disease, they can cause symptoms in other parts of the body. This might include joint pain, skin problems, eye issues or mouth ulcers. Nearly half of people with Crohn’s or Colitis experience these symptoms. There may be times when symptoms are better and other times when they’re worse, known as flare-ups. Having a flare-up can be a difficult time and have a big impact on a person's life. It can be hard to cope with the symptoms, but what’s often overlooked is the impact the conditions can have on a person’s mental health. People living with Crohn’s or Colitis may be twice as likely to experience mental health problems, like anxiety and depression. Want to get involved in myth-busting this World IBD Day? There are more than 500,000 people in the UK living with Crohn’s or Colitis. That's 25,000 people a year who are given the life changing diagnosis of Inflammatory Bowel Disease. It’s a sizeable chunk of the population, but despite this, there are often myths and misconceptions surrounding these conditions, which feed stigmas, hinder understanding, and undermine the severity of symptoms experienced by those living with Crohn's or Colitis. That's why, in the run up to World IBD Day, we’re highlighting some of the most popular misconceptions people have about Crohn’s and Colitis and setting the record straight. Have you ever found yourself in a conversation where you're met with the myth - 'It's not that bad, it's just a dodgy tummy right?'. Crohn’s and Colitis involves chronic inflammation of the gut, which can lead to damage and ulcers. When your gut doesn’t work properly, the effects can be devastating. Crohn’s and Colitis can disrupt every part of your life - from digestion and joints to your energy levels and mental health. There can also be severe complications such as strictures (narrowing of the intestines), fistulas (abnormal connections between different parts of the intestines or between the intestines and other organs) and abscesses – all of which are incredibly painful. Often people living with Crohn’s or Colitis describe the intense pain as ‘someone tying their innards in a knot’. This World IBD Day 🌍 help us correct the widespread misunderstanding, so no one feels ignored or dismissed because of their Crohn's or Colitis. Living with IBD can feel like a constant balancing act. Low fibre diets might help manage symptoms, but then weight gain creeps in - frustrating if it’s unwanted. Calorie deficit screams from every weight loss article, but uncontrollable hunger makes that near impossible when eating a low fibre diet.  Sound familiar? You’re not alone!  Many with low-fibre IBD struggle with: 👉 Increased hunger: Low fibre can leave you feeling unsatisfied, leading to overeating. 👉 Fast Food Frenzy: Convenience often means processed foods, low in fibre and high in calories. 👉 Blood Sugar Rollercoaster: Low fibre can lead to blood sugar spikes, further fueling hunger pangs. 👉 Nutrient Deficiencies: Processed, low-fibre options often lack essential nutrients. But here’s the good news: Managing weight with IBD is possible!  Here’s your action plan: 🫶 Fibre that loves you back: Find the right fibre for YOU. Talk to your doctor or a nutritionist for a personalized plan. 🏋️‍♀️ Move It, Move It!: Exercise is crucial for weight management and overall well-being. Choose activities you enjoy and consult with a doctor or trainer about modifications for your limitations. 💤 Sleep & Stress Savvy: Both sleep and stress can impact weight. Prioritize quality sleep and healthy stress management techniques. Ready to ditch the “catch-22” and create a weight management plan that works for YOUR IBD? 🙂 Don’t just dream it, achieve it!  Comment “FIBRE” below or DM me for a personalized approach that considers your limitations. Endometriosis is a systemic disorder 💛 Colonoscopy vs Sigmoidoscopy aka flexible colonoscopy 🔬🚽💩 Note: everyone’s experience is different. Tell me yours below ⬇️  I had my first colonoscopy back in 2021 for endo and I was in an agony 💔despite having loads of sedation, gas and painkillers. All results were clear however I had load is adhisons and scar tissue around my large intestines that was a contributor factor to unbearable, pain during the procedure. In February, my MRI showed abnormal intestines, so my gastrologist said I need a new camera test however I did not want it to go through the same awful experience. After he assessed the MRI he suggested taking flexible colonoscopy test, which only goes to a section of large bowel and the bonus was I didn’t needed any bowel prep medication 💩. The experience was amazing. The doctor and the hospital did everything in their control to make my day as easy as possible I was about looked after and I did not remember anything from the procedure at all. The results are not back yet and he took a handful of biopsies for lab test. I don’t have my symptoms from my gut but they wanted to rule out what they saw on the MRI scan just to check . Are you in a calorie deficit but not losing weight?  As well as looking at how much you’re eating, are you considering what you’re eating?  Chronic inflammation can stem not only from inflammatory diseases but also from excess sugar and refined carbs.  Making whole foods your priority will help to prevent gut inflammation.  What is a whole food? Something that’s a singular ingredient (killed or grown). Work on an 80:20 balance to allow for some flexibility for other foods - this ensures that you can make it a forever and sustainable diet and more of a lifestyle change opposed to a short-period diet.  Key foods to include in your 80% ▪️ Protein - original sourced meats, poultry, fish, eggs, legumes, seeds & nuts etc.  ▪️ Healthy fats - oily fish, nuts, olive oil, seeds, avocado, eggs, coconut, tofu, dark chocolate etc.  ▪️ Wholegrains - Quinoa, oats, brown rice, buckwheat, lentils, chickpeas, kidney beans etc. ▪️ Vegetables - leafy greens, broccoli, tomatoes, carrots, mushrooms, onions, peppers, kale, cauliflower etc. ▪️ Fruits - strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, cherries, apples, pomegranate, citrus fruits etc  Also herbs & spices have great anti inflammatory properties including: ginger, numeric, cayenne pepper, cinnamon, garlic, black pepper, clove, rosemary, cardamon, oregano, thyme, basil, cumin etc  When your body isn’t fighting inflammation, it functions optimally, making it easier for you to achieve and maintain a healthy weight 💪🏼 Follow me for nutritional guidance and meal inspiration  #antiinflammatorydiet #antiinflammatoryfood #pcosdiet #thyroiddiet #chronicinflammation #colitis #guthealth #healthyliving #wholefoods

👋 My name is Aliz, and I’m a health and fitness coach recently also exercise referral qualified coach and gut health specialist, but most importantly, a mom of two who’s been through it. Living with a chronic condition (I was diagnosed in 2012) can make you feel like “normal” is out of reach.  We all want things like: ➡️Steady energy levels to keep up with life ➡️A healthy relationship with food that fuels your body, not fear ➡️Freedom from pain and the constant bathroom worry ➡️Confidence to reach fitness goals for ourselves, not just because of illness I get it. I’ve been there. ‍After my diagnosis, I transformed my lifestyle and achieved remission for 6 years! But life throws curveballs (newborns!), and I had a setback.  But I didn’t give up. Why?  Because I knew what felt possible. I dedicated myself to studying holistic approaches backed by research that doctors often don’t mention.  These tools helped me and countless clients to: ✅ Feel amazing! Reduce symptoms and regain control. ✅ Build strength, both body and mind. Crush challenges and reach goals. ✅ Find a supportive community. Connect with people who understand and inspire you. Ready to ditch the “I’m sick and tired” feeling and take charge of your health?  Let’s do this together! Everyone in the UK now 😂 We all know that a little sunshine can make a world of difference, especially for our mental health and managing chronic illnesses.  Here are some benefits of sunshine: 💜 Boosts mood and combats depression 💜 Enhances vitamin D production 💜 Supports immune function 💜 Reduces inflammation 💜 Improves sleep quality ❗️For those with IBD, RA, lupus and people who take Azathioprine, it’s crucial to be cautious, as it increases sun sensitivity and the risk of skin cancers.  Even if you’re not on meds, it’s essential to get sunshine safely: 🤌 Use high SPF sunscreen 🤌 Wear thin, protective clothing 🤌 Take short, frequent walks 🤌 Soak up the sun responsibly and enjoy its benefits! 👉 Follow @thechronicallyfitcoach for more tips on managing chronic conditions holistically. This pic was the " it's time so sort my shit out" moment. This was 2022 just after I had my second baby. I hated myself. The way my clothes didn't fit me. My mahooosive gunt. Just everything. This was all fine sort of as I had just popped out my second child so I didn't want to be too hard on myself but I was so stuck and didn't know what to do. I was so low. I developed postnatal depression when my boy was around 6 weeks old. I didn't know I had it but it was my close family and friends that could notice how I wasn't coping. I bonded well with him but I just couldn't cope with the lack of sleep I had insomnia and could barely survive or eat a decent meal etc it was so so hard. So after visiting the Dr they gave me some meds to help me out with a bit of serotonin. Which was doing its magic ✨  At this exact time I was also diagnosed with Colitis which is fucking grim! 🩸 My consultant said my colitis and mental health come hand in hand so when I am stressed my tummy flares up. They want me on steroids but I refused and said I can manage this myself by practicing wellness and mindfulness along with the serotonin boost 😉 your gut is linked directly to your brain. So if you can sort your head out your gut will follow. It was around this time I signed up with quite possibly one of the best coaches out there @chloepickford_ifbbpro to help me get out of this rut. In this pic above I weighed 111kg which is almost 17.5 stone. Since being with Chloe I have lost around 30kg which is 4.7 stone. She has been there for me through thick and thin. All my health issues with my conditions, mental health and all other fucks life throws at you along the way. If anyone is considering getting a coach just do it you won't regret it. Travelling with GI conditions IS possible! ✨ Like I said in the video, although I'm a dietitian I definitely don't have it all figured out! But here are a few thoughts and considerations before your next trip. The main thing I would say is to be prepared (which the scouts have been saying for decades 🤣)! 1. Translate key phrases about your condition before you go. This can be on paper, on your phone or you can buy cards which have key phrases on for some conditions. 2. Know you can get access to the internet for a translate app for when they reply (it's one thing saying a sentence but it will need a conversation) so either using mobile data or WiFi 3. Search for gluten free recommendations in the place you are going. Some cities/countries do gluten free really well! If you haven't travelled much since diagnosis, maybe start with some places you know will be able to cater for you (I have been to 100% gluten free places in major cities in France, Italy, Hungry and Austria. 4. Choose familiar foods. I know this can be frustrating for the foodies who want to experience local cuisine and if you feel confident and happy choosing unfamiliar foods then that's perfect! But if you're a little worried picking foods you have a lot at home can be a good shout (for me this is fresh fish, rice/potatoes and veggies ALTHOUGH remember to ask about preparation/cross contamination and look out for sauces especially soy sauce if you're gluten free!) 5. Have hand sanitizer and tissue/toilet roll with you. Like I said my dodgy stomach wasn't coeliac related on my last trip but so many toilets in Colombia did not have toilet roll, a sink or soap! Better to be over prepared than caught without! 6. TAKE FOOD. If you don't know that there will be safe options take some high energy basics with you. I tend to take a few types of crackers (out of the box to save space), trail mix/ nuts and raisins, biscuits and depending on the packing situation, bread. I have taken a bread roll into a restaurant before and asked for butter. 7. Say no. Refuse food. Send it back. Advocate for yourself.  For me one of the worst things about being coeliac is feeling like I'm an inconvenience or that I'm being awkward. WE ARE NOT. It is the lovely waiting staffs JOB to help us and we are doing it for our health not  to be picky/awkward. I'm very lucky that my friends advocate for me too (they send food back and have asked local bus drivers to pull over when I wasn't well). If you are travelling with people open up to them, they can have your back which can mean so much in the moments you're finding it difficult to advocate for yourself. Is there anything that you do that I've missed?  Let me know in the comments 👇 #glutenfreetravel #coeliactravel #celiactravel #gastrointestinalproblems  #IBD #IBS #crohns #colitis #travellersbest

The judgement around being overweight & having stomach issues!  I understand loosing alot of weight is a major symptom which I am not putting down or brushing off as its hard to cope with (I'm currently going through this myself recently) ... but the ghosting I've had when I was bigger is concerning.  I had one nurse say I couldn't be that bad if I've not lost weight, I remember it clear as day in A&E. I think this was just a brush off comment to try & make me feel better, but it didn't! wound me up more than anything, then I had emergency surgery for a stoma.  just irritates the hell out of me 😅 anyone else the same?  I get it, you put crap food in your body you're going to feel bad before anyone comments that. We are talking about inflammatory bowel disease, I have a really good diet now and loosing alot of weight due to crohns symptoms, so I do get both ends of the spectrum. Travelling with GI conditions IS possible! ✨ Like I said in the video, although I'm a dietitian I definitely don't have it all figured out! But here are a few thoughts and considerations before your next trip. The main thing I would say is to be prepared (which the scouts have been saying for decades 🤣)! 1. Translate key phrases about your condition before you go. This can be on paper, on your phone or you can buy cards which have key phrases on for some conditions. 2. Know you can get access to the internet for a translate app for when they reply (it's one thing saying a sentence but it will need a conversation) so either using mobile data or WiFi 3. Search for gluten free recommendations in the place you are going. Some cities/countries do gluten free really well! If you haven't travelled much since diagnosis, maybe start with some places you know will be able to cater for you (I have been to 100% gluten free places in major cities in France, Italy, Hungry and Austria. 4. Choose familiar foods. I know this can be frustrating for the foodies who want to experience local cuisine and if you feel confident and happy choosing unfamiliar foods then that's perfect! But if you're a little worried picking foods you have a lot at home can be a good shout (for me this is fresh fish, rice/potatoes and veggies ALTHOUGH remember to ask about preparation/cross contamination and look out for sauces especially soy sauce if you're gluten free!) 5. Have hand sanitizer and tissue/toilet roll with you. Like I said my dodgy stomach wasn't coeliac related on my last trip but so many toilets in Colombia did not have toilet roll, a sink or soap! Better to be over prepared than caught without! 6. TAKE FOOD. If you don't know that there will be safe options take some high energy basics with you. I tend to take a few types of crackers (out of the box to save space), trail mix/ nuts and raisins, biscuits and depending on the packing situation, bread. I have taken a bread roll into a restaurant before and asked for butter. 7. Say no. Refuse food. Send it back. Advocate for yourself.  For me one of the worst things about being coeliac is feeling like I'm an inconvenience or that I'm being awkward. WE ARE NOT. It is the lovely waiting staffs JOB to help us and we are doing it for our health not  to be picky/awkward. I'm very lucky that my friends advocate for me too (they send food back and have asked local bus drivers to pull over when I wasn't well). If you are travelling with people open up to them, they can have your back which can mean so much in the moments you're finding it difficult to advocate for yourself. Is there anything that you do that I've missed?  Let me know in the comments 👇 #glutenfreetravel #coeliactravel #celiactravel #gastrointestinalproblems  #IBD #IBS #crohns #colitis #travellersbest

IBD Myth: You can’t travel with Crohn’s Disease!! New York, Morocco & Egypt all within the past year! Saying you can’t travel is such a myth and I’ll give you my best travel tips in this post. But first, I’ll be honest with you, before I got married I would NEVER travel and would use my Crohn’s Disease as an excuse! But now, I can’t seem to stop travelling! Yes there are still a lot of things I worry about when travelling- the biggest one is the availability of toilets - but you can’t let life pass you by! So what can you do to make travelling easier with IBD: 1. Plan Ahead: Research your destination for accessible toilets and medical facilities.  2.Pack Essentials:Bring your medications, a doctor’s note, extra supplies, and some non-perishable snacks that are safe for your diet. 3.Choose Accommodations Wisely:Opt for places that have easy access to toilets and kitchen facilities if you need to prepare your own meals. 4. Stay Hydrated: Dehydration can worsen symptoms, so always carry water with you. 5. Get Travel Insurance: Ensure your insurance covers pre-existing conditions and any potential flare-ups while abroad. Have you ever been told meat rots in your gut?  That it’s hard to digest?  That you need fibre for healthy bowels?  This is all completely false.  The only foods that reach your colon intact are plants.  Meat is fully broken down to liquid before it goes into the colon.  So how is it “hard to digest”?   How is it going to “rot in your gut”?  It’s time to wake up and realise everything we have been told is a lie.  If you have issues with your digestion/bowels.  Ditch the plant fibre and up the meat! Let me explain… Many of you may have heard the terms IBD and IBS being interchanged for one another as if they were the same thing. While it is true that both present with similar symptoms, can be triggered by similar things, they are however not the same. IBD is classified as an actual disease that causes intestinal destruction due to inflammation while IBS is defined as a syndrome, or a disorder of gut function brought about by the control of the gut-brain axis (GBA). Furthermore, the differences don’t stop there as you can see IBD when diagnostic imaging (x-ray, CT, MRI, and ultrasound scans) are used whereas you can’t see IBS on these scans and IBD is associated with an increased risk of developing colon cancer whereas IBS is not. Even though symptoms of IBS (bloating, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, and constipation) are like IBD, there are so many other features that separate the two. For example, IBD is associated with fatigue, weight loss, generally feeling unwell, loss of appetite as well as mouth ulcers whereas none of these are present in IBS. The most obvious difference between the two is that the ‘inflammation’ in IBS does not cause destructive damage to the intestines in addition to there is no bleeding after bowel movements in IBS unlike in IBD further differentiating the two. For me I’ve had so many MRI scans but the truth is I never really have gotten used to them even though I know what to expect. But for those of you who haven’t had one and are wondering what to expect here’s a little explanation: Preparation: You might need to fast or follow specific dietary instructions. This will help ensure there’s nothing in your bowel that could be mistaken for an abnormality in the images or that could hide important findings. Contrast Dye:I had a cannula inserted as I need intravenous contrast so my blood vessels and blood supply to my organs can be seen. I also had to drink a manitol solution (which is not very pleasant) so my bowel can be seen in more detail. The Scan: This bit is okish. Once you get over the sense of claustrophobia I tend to try and have a nap or keep my eyes closed. Results: Once the doctors review your images then they will be able to inform the IBD team of what’s going on. ⬇️ Crohns Talk part 3 ⬇️  Painful truth is the NHS don't really care about your health as much as you think.  They're going to forever stick to their script depending on how urgent things really are and yet you're still going to wait months , maybe even years to get what you need...all while you're supposed to be carrying on with life on the daily  Weather you're new to the whole illness thing or currently at that point where you're fed up , start taking action for yourself where you can  Are you hydrated enough on the daily - add electrolytes and salts to foods to help  How's your diet - multiple studies show whole food diets can improve many illnesses, rashes , flare ups etc...key word being improve not fix before the know it all's pipe up 'DIET DOESN'T CURE ME'  Are you exercising, getting your steps/cardio in , daily morning sunlight and the biggest one for me and should be for others, are you managing your stress levels.  'Improve' in all these sections before things start getting bad and you're giving yourself a much higher percentage of staying or getting into remission quicker and not needing as many things the hospitals offer on their little script of theirs  What's your thoughts on the system or how they've treat your situation? #ileostomy #crohns #ibd #NHS #stomabag #ibs #colostomybag #colitis

⬇️ Crohns Talk Part 5 ⬇️ What gets you through the hard days? Fatigued, flaring , cramps, sickness? If you're reading this and have crohns you know what I mean and you might not know it but you've probably already faced some of your worst days without even knowing it Some of you still would of went to work , looked after people , cooked meals ect all while struggling...pretty bad a** if you ask me And when those days roll back round you now know you're strong enough to do it all again To those who may be newly diagnosed you might think 'man this is hard' after the first hardship, only to find out in a years time let's say that it was all just a learning curve life lesson Pain teaches you many things, take it all on board , ask yourself how you feeling during these hard times and how you can overcome it for future days Like I said at the start of this , what gets you through the hard days? Is it a person , a job , a hobby, discipline? Whatever it is , keep it close to you and think about that whenever days feel hard as soon enough you'll be back feeling yourself , doing your thing 👊🏻💜 #crohns #ibd #stomabag ##crohnsandcolitis #colitis #ibs  #gym #motivation

➡️Crohns Talk Part 4⬅️ UNPOPULAR OPINION 🤔💭  🚨F**k the IG/TT Crohns Gurus 🚨  They'v come out to play again with some questionable posts so here's my opinion Most these people tend to always be ill , out of shape pretty lazy preaching to others with things like  ➡️ It's okay to be ill ➡️ Gym won't help you ➡️ Diet won't help you ➡️ Seek 'professional' help  Could go on forever with other things that they say too🫠  And it's the people who are down bad and ill or new to everything that tends to listen to them  Why...?  If you just went against everything they try push on you through a fancy caption that is colour coordinatored for their IG feed you'd be giving yourself a head start in getting over your symptoms meaning when you go get 'professional' help' (they love that saying) you're one or more steps ahead 🤯 It's as if they get a buzz out of seeing people do bad or be at their level...ill and uncappble  Imagine being ill as f**k and instead of accepting it as that's normal...you manage to go for a walk , hit a 20 minute gym sesh , drink an extra litre of water...whatever it might be as well as bringing someone up to do the same imagine how good you and others would feel?  Depression for example you wouldn't tell a mate 'ah embrace it , have a lazy day eat ice cream , get some sleep' etc  You'd be round at his house , encouraging him to do something, keep busy take your mind away from things , get the momentum going.  It's the exact same with crohns , at somepoint you have to stand up to yourself and make change as no is going to do it for you No ones asking you to gym 7x a week , climb a mountain and break some records daily...  Just a case of bettering yourself every day and giving yourself that edge whenever you can  What's it to be , sit around doing nothing telling people they're ill like me OR actually trying to make something of your situation as let's be honest these so called professionals ain't going to be running to you to fix your case  Happy Sunday...f**k the Gurus #TeamShitBag 👊🏻 #crohns #colitis #ibd #ibs #colostomy #ileostomy #crohnsandcolitis #crohnscolitis #stoma #stomabag

Is it a person , a job , a hobby, discipline? DONT DO BARBELL ROWS! They won't hit the lats/upper back properly as it isn't stable, you can't get a good mind to muscle connection, can't get a 56 second eccentric causing MAXIMUM muscle gain. All you're doing is boosting your ego and making noise as well as taking up a sqaut rack Literally just do whatever you enjoy... Id love to see it proven somewhere but I'd love to see two people's comparisons of a chest supported Tbar Row and Barbell rows to a natural over the space of 3-5 years just to see how little the changes are between the two Go with whatever your gym has , whatever you enjoy and whatever feels good 💪🏻 Reason I do them is I feel like I can overload it better over time compared to any other similar row. Plus I quite like having stablising muscles getting worked too as over time they'll be getting stronger (spinal erectors/core). Finally is every gym has one so it's easy to stick to a plan 🤷‍♂️ #barbell #backday #bodybuilding #dorianyates #crohns #exercises #colitis #ibd

Your skin might be telling a story too! 🦋✨  Many with inflammatory bowel disease experience skin conditions like psoriasis or eczema due to inflammation and immune response.  Remember, your skin is a reflection of your overall health! 💖 Here are some tips to help manage skin conditions while living with IBD: Hydrate, Hydrate, Hydrate! 💧: Keep your skin hydrated with plenty of water and a good moisturizer to maintain skin barrier health. Gentle Skincare Routine 🧴: Opt for fragrance-free, hypoallergenic products to avoid irritation. Stick to gentle cleansers and moisturizers that soothe rather than strip your skin. Sun Protection ☀️: Protect your skin from harmful UV rays. Use sunscreen daily, especially if you’re on medications that increase sun sensitivity. Balanced Diet 🥗: Focus on an anti-inflammatory diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and omega-3 fatty acids. A healthy diet can benefit both your gut and skin health. Stress Management 🧘‍♀️: Stress can exacerbate both IBD and skin conditions. Incorporate relaxation techniques like yoga, meditation, or deep breathing exercises into your routine. Consult a Dermatologist 👩‍⚕️: If you’re experiencing persistent skin issues, seek professional advice. A dermatologist can provide tailored treatments to help manage your skin concerns. Stay Informed 📚: Educate yourself about the link between IBD and skin health. Knowledge is power, and understanding your body can help you advocate for yourself better. Let’s raise awareness and support each other in this journey! With funding from Crohn’s and Colitis UK, researchers at Aston University have developed a new digital support programme for young people living with IBD, called ASSIST-IBD. The programme has been designed with young people with IBD to help others follow their treatment plan. The programme contains activities and podcasts tackling tricky topics such as  💊Taking medication 👩‍⚕️Talking to healthcare professionals 💤Following lifestyle advice  💬Telling others about your IBD You can access ASSIST-IBD online 💻📱 In each topic you will be supported to set a goal to overcome a challenge you face. We are now looking for young people to try out ASSIST-IBD for 6-12 weeks and tell us what it is like to use. We are also interested in parents/guardians’ views of our parent resources.  To explain this project in more detail we are hosting an information evening on Thursday 12th September 2024 at 6-7pm. During the event you will be able to ask the research team questions about the project. This event is free to attend and open to young people (aged 13-17) who have been diagnosed with IBD and live in the UK as well as parents/guardians of young people (aged 13-17) who have been diagnosed with IBD and live in the UK To join the event, scan the QR code or use this link https://astonpsychology.eu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0vOvyGDI0dSZAB8  ASSIST-IBD, co-designed by young people with IBD, for young people with IBD! 💜💜💜💜💜 #crohnsdisease #crohns #colitis #inflammatoryboweldisease #ibd #WorldIBDDay #research #IBDtreatment #lovetheskinyourein #crohnsdiseaseawareness #crohnsurvivor #ChronicIllness #invisibleillness #ibdawareness #ibdwarrior #crohnswarriors #notalldisabilitiesarevisible #crohnsandcolitis #guthealthforlife #autoimmune #autoimmunedisease #awareness #advice #help #honesty #allinforcrohnsandcolitis #ibdscotland #crohnsscotland #colitisscotland

Do you have iron deficiency anaemia?  Save this post and follow for IBD facts and taboo breaking chats! Did you know that around 1 in 3 individuals with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) experience iron deficiency anemia?  Causes include chronic blood loss and impaired absorption due to inflammation.  This can lead to fatigue and impact quality of life. Management often involves intravenous iron therapy for effective treatment. Crohns Talk Part 6 | Mental Challenges If dealing with your crohns , stoma , health physically or mentally I highly suggest starting the gym or even a sport...hear me out  When I was first getting diagnosed at 15 was probably the worst for me , didn't want to do anything with friends , family didn't understand, I'd go to school sit alone in a room , do my exams and leave just to fall asleep when home as I felt that ill and drained and fed up of everything. Only thing I looked forward to when I could take part was playing football For the 1-2hrs of playing that , your mind switches off completely. Your health is fine , you're relaxed, tiredness not so bad , everything just seems to improve. All because your brain blocks it out to focus on what you enjoy Spending that time with a bunch of people to take your off to really helps as you can laugh/joke around , you can chat to them , they'll ask you questions.  Especially in a team sport they want to know if they can help and will try to understand you Moral of the post is find something you enjoy and run with it. Even if it gives you that piece of mind for a small amount of time , your body will thank it's for being in that calmer state of mind as me personally and a few others I know stress is like a fire for the body and mind making little problems 10x worse And if you happen to think 'ah I don't have a hobbie'. Just go for a walk with some of your favourite music playing or if possible with friend and talk about whatever comes to mind , you'll get the exact same state of mind Things will get better #crohns #stoma #health #mindset #ibd #ibs #colitis

Having a lifelong condition like Crohn’s or Colitis means you get to know the NHS very well, and Lord Darzi’s report highlights the challenges that members of our community tell us about every day. Over 500,000 people in the UK are living with Crohn’s and colitis, with many facing delays at every turn, risking further serious complications to their health. A lack of support for addressing patient needs is leading to frustration for NHS staff and those they treat. People with Crohn’s and Colitis don’t want to be stuck on waiting lists, they want to be out living their lives. We all know that there’s no quick fix for the NHS, but we welcome Lord Darzi’s report and the UK Government’s promise to turn our health service around. The patient voice must be put at the heart of these reforms. It's pain awareness month, Crohn's and Colitis do not just affect the gut, they can cause problems in other parts of the body, called extraintestinal manifestations or EIMs. Joint problems are one of the most common types of EIM related to Crohn’s or Colitis. Recent studies have found that up to 46 in every 100 people with Crohn’s or Colitis may experience joint problems. Key facts: 🦵Joint problems can include joint pain and swelling in the joints in your back, hands, feet, arms and legs. 🦵Spondyloarthritis is a group of inflammatory arthritis conditions. This means your immune system has caused damage in your joints. Having Crohn's or Colitis can increase your risk of developing spondyloarthritis. 🦵Joint problems can come and go. For some people they get worse when your Crohn’s or Colitis is worse. For others, you may have a flare-up of arthritis symptoms with no gut symptoms. 🦵If left untreated, some arthritis conditions can lead to permanent damage. Speak to your GP or IBD team if you have pain, swelling or stiffness in your joints. 🦵Medicine treatments, exercise and physiotherapy can all be helpful in managing joint problems. To find out more about joint problems related to Crohn’s or Colitis, go to our link in bio, under 'Information on Crohn's & Colitis' click 'Joint Pain' #Crohns #Colitis #InflammatoryBowelDisease #IBD #JointPain #PainAwarenessMonth #PainAwareness
